2610.08268.title: DySCo: Dynamic Sharding for Collaborative Edge-Cloud LLM Inference with Depth-Synchronized Batching
2610.08268.paper_summary: Pervasive intelligent applications are increasingly deployed on mobile and Internet of Things (IoT) edge devices. Consequently, Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support these applications. Yet, due to their high resource demands, LLMs are mostly deployed in the cloud. Layer-wise edge-cloud inference lets resource-constrained edge devices contribute computation to LLMs they cannot host in full. However, heterogeneous split points introduce two coupled inefficiencies. First, edge execution and communication create idle gaps between cloud invocations. Second, requests arriving at different model depths cannot be conventionally batched. We present DySCo, a collaborative runtime that keeps KV caches local and introduces dyForward, a model-aware layer-range executor that runs configurable contiguous layer ranges from resident model shards without reloading weights. For multi-edge serving settings, we introduce depth-synchronized batching (DSB), which advances heterogeneous requests to the deepest cut and batches their common suffix. Experiments across heterogeneous devices, two model families, and local and wide-area links show that idle gaps increase the latency of subsequent GPU forward calls even when waiting time is excluded, adding up to 25 ms of additional cloud-side suffix latency per decoding step in our measurements. At an average concurrency of eight, DSB improves throughput by 275% over FIFO, 48% over exact-match batching, and 79% over round-robin interleaving while reducing mean per-session latency. Together, these results show that requests with different edge-cloud splits can reuse resident cloud weights and share batched suffix computation. The artifact repository for this work is publicly available at: https://github.com/Large-scale-Sustainable-Computing-LSC/dysco-artifact
2610.08268.paper_summary_zh: 普遍的智能應用越來越多地部署在移動設備和物聯網 (IoT) 邊緣設備上。<lb/>因此，大型語言模型 (LLMs) 越來越多地用於支持這些應用。<lb/>然而，由於其高資源需求，LLMs 大多數是部署在雲端。<lb/>逐層的邊緣-雲推理讓資源受限的邊緣設備能夠對它們無法完全承載的 LLMs 進行計算貢獻。<lb/>然而，異質的切分點引入了兩種相互關聯的低效。<lb/>首先，邊緣執行和通信在雲端調用之間產生了空閒間隙。<lb/>其次，抵達不同模型深度的請求無法按照傳統方式進行批處理。<lb/>我們提出了 DySCo，一個協作運行時，將 KV 緩存保持在本地，並引入了 dyForward，一個模型感知的層範圍執行器，能夠從常駐模型分片中運行可配置的連續層範圍，而無需重新加載權重。<lb/>對於多邊緣服務設置，我們引入了深度同步批處理 (DSB)，它將異質請求推進到最深的切分點並批處理它們的公共後綴。<lb/>在異質設備、兩個模型系列以及本地和廣域鏈路上的實驗顯示，即使在排除等待時間的情況下，空閒間隙也會增加隨後 GPU 前向調用的延遲，在我們的測量中，每個解碼步驟增加了最多 25 毫秒的額外雲端後綴延遲。<lb/>在平均八個並發的情況下，DSB 的吞吐量比 FIFO 提高了 275%，比精確匹配批處理提高了 48%，比輪詢交錯提高了 79%，同時減少了每會話的平均延遲。<lb/>綜合這些結果顯示，具有不同邊緣-雲切分的請求可以重用常駐雲端權重並共享批處理後綴計算。<lb/>本工作的文物庫可在以下網址公開獲得：https://github.com/Large-scale-Sustainable-Computing-LSC/dysco-artifact
